# Goal: Agnostic Skill Evaluation & Versioning Harness (SEVH)

**Purpose.** Stand up a harness-agnostic system that *measurably and verifiably* improves Luke's agent skills, proves the improvement across model releases / thinking levels / cheap models, version-controls every change with evidence, and serves the right skill **variant** to each provider/model automatically. This is a *continual* loop, not a one-shot.

**How to use this doc.**
- §A is the copy-paste **goal prompt** — feed it to a `/goal` run (or `create_goal`).
- §B–§I are the spec the prompt references: success definition, acceptance, measurement, architecture, phases, constraints, the final verification drill, risks.
- Appendix = grounded tool/command reference (real paths) so the executing agent doesn't hallucinate the tooling.

**Status:** spec authored; build not started. Pilot skill TBD (recommend `development/verify-this` or `code-review` — both already have eval scaffolding).

---

## §A — The Goal Prompt (paste this)

> Build the **Agnostic Skill Evaluation & Versioning Harness (SEVH)** described in `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-agnostic-skill-eval-harness.md`. Work phase by phase (§F); each phase ships a deliverable **and** its verification before the next starts. Do not claim a phase done without the evidence named in its "Verify" line.
>
> The harness must let me, with one command per step: (1) evaluate any skill across a **model matrix** — ≥1 frontier, ≥1 mid, ≥1 cheap/small model, ≥2 thinking levels, plus newly-released models added as a one-line matrix cell with **zero code changes**; (2) score each rollout with **deterministic assertions first, then validated LLM judges** (single + `fuse` ensemble), producing a comparable scorecard (quality, pass-rate, cost/tokens, latency per cell); (3) generate a candidate skill edit (`skillopt train`), evaluate it against baseline, and get a **VERIFIED / NOT VERIFIED / INCONCLUSIVE** verdict gated on the thresholds in §D; (4) maintain **≥2 versions/variants of a skill** (e.g. full + lite) that load/switch **automatically** based on the active provider/model/thinking level, with **prompt-cache stability preserved**; (5) record every promoted version in **version control with its scorecard as evidence** via `skill-workshop` → git; and (6) run the whole thing as a **continual autoresearch loop** that auto-reverts regressions.
>
> Success = the §C acceptance checklist passes end-to-end for one real pilot skill, measured exactly as §D specifies, and the §H verification drill is green. Honor the §G non-negotiables (agnostic contract, cache golden rule, progressive disclosure, no improvement claim without a committed scorecard + VERIFIED verdict, deterministic-before-judge, CLI/script wrappers for every recurring action). Reuse existing tooling (`evals`, `skill-optimizer`/`scripts/skillopt`, `skillos`, `harness-loop` eval-gate, `autoresearch-*`, `pi-workflow`, `fuse`, `ultracode`, `ctx`, `skill-workshop`) — extend, don't reinvent. Extend the existing `skill-loader` with a **load-time variant resolver** in the `skill` tool (track model via `session_start`/`ctx.model` + `model_select`, thinking via `pi.getThinkingLevel()`); do **not** build a new tool or touch core — keep the `<available_skills>` listing byte-stable, vary only the loaded body. When all phases are green, write the runbook (§F Phase 5) and report the final scorecard.

---

## §B — Definition of success (the outcome)

The system is successful when Luke can run a **repeatable, version-controlled, model-agnostic loop** that:

1. Takes any skill and a **model matrix** and returns a **comparable scorecard** per cell (quality score, pass-rate, cost, latency).
2. Tells him, with a single non-hedged verdict, whether a proposed skill change is a **real improvement** (VERIFIED) or not — backed by numbers, not vibes.
3. Ships **multiple variants of a skill** (e.g. full for frontier, lite for cheap/low-thinking) that the harness **auto-selects at session start** by active provider/model/thinking level — without breaking prompt cache.
4. Records every promoted version as a **git commit + committed scorecard + skill-workshop proposal with evidence**, so the improvement history is auditable across model releases.
5. **Absorbs a new model release** by adding one matrix cell and re-running — no code edits — proving genuine agnosticism.
6. Runs **continually**: an autoresearch session drives candidate → eval → verdict → promote/revert, and the regression gate prevents backsliding over time.

"Done" is not "code exists." Done is: the §C checklist is green for one **real pilot skill**, end-to-end, with the §D evidence committed to the repo.

---

## §C — Acceptance checklist (every item needs concrete evidence)

| # | Requirement | Evidence that proves it |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Agnostic eval contract exists | `eval-record.schema.json` + at least 2 harness adapters (pi headless; Claude-Code via `ultracode`) emit the same record shape; a 3rd adapter could be added without touching the runner |
| C2 | Rubric + gold cases for pilot skill | `eval/<skill>/rubric.md` + `cases/{train,val,test}.jsonl` (≥10 labeled cases, deterministic assertions present) |
| C3 | Validated judge(s) | Judge passes TPR ≥ 0.9 **and** TNR ≥ 0.9 on held-out test split; `fuse` ensemble panel ≥ best single judge on same labels; confusion matrix committed |
| C4 | Model matrix runs | `matrix.yaml` with ≥3 model cells (frontier/mid/cheap) × ≥2 thinking levels; runner produces a scorecard for the pilot across all cells |
| C5 | New-model agnosticism | Adding one cell to `matrix.yaml` and re-running yields a valid scorecard with **zero code changes** (demonstrated in the §H drill) |
| C6 | Verifiable improvement | One candidate edit returns **VERIFIED** per §D thresholds; one deliberately-bad candidate returns **NOT VERIFIED** and is auto-reverted by the regression gate |
| C7 | Dynamic skill variants | ≥2 variants of the pilot skill; contract eval proves the correct variant loads per model-class/thinking level and that same-model sessions stay byte-stable (cache canary) |
| C8 | Version control + provenance | Promoted version = git commit linking the committed scorecard + autoresearch run id + judge verdict, applied through `skill-workshop` (proposal carries `evidenceRefs`) |
| C9 | Continual loop | An `autoresearch` session (`autoresearch.sh` scorer + `autoresearch.checks.sh` gate + `autoresearch.jsonl` ledger) runs the full candidate→eval→verdict→promote/revert cycle unattended for ≥3 iterations |
| C10 | Cost/efficiency measured | Per-cell tokens + $ recorded; a cheap-cell variant shows quality within ε of full at materially lower cost (≥30% fewer tokens) — or the gap is reported honestly |
| C11 | Adherence via CLI | Every recurring action (scaffold, run-matrix, score, promote, new-model drill) is a script/wrapper with `--help`, dry-run, and JSON output; no step requires remembering a raw incantation |
| C12 | Runbook + docs | `docs/` runbook covers create-skill-eval, run-matrix, read-scorecard, promote, add-model, author-variant; wired into `weekly-review` for the continual cadence |

---

## §D — How improvement is measured (no vibes)

**Per-cell composite quality score** `∈ [0,1]`, per (skill_version × matrix_cell):
```
composite = 0.6 * deterministic_assertion_pass_rate   # schema, expected_refs, must/ must-not mention, tool args, exit codes
          + 0.4 * validated_judge_rubric_score         # only judges that passed C3 may contribute
```
Weights tunable per skill, **deterministic must dominate**. Run `n ≥ 5` rollouts per (version × cell) to absorb nondeterminism; report mean ± spread.

**Improvement verdict** (from `development/verify-this` — VERIFIED / NOT VERIFIED / INCONCLUSIVE). A candidate is **VERIFIED** iff *all* hold:
- target-cell composite delta ≥ **+0.05** (or the skill-specific threshold declared in its rubric), with baseline mean and candidate mean spreads non-overlapping at n≥5;
- **no** non-target cell regresses by > **0.02**;
- deterministic contracts remain **100%** (any contract break ⇒ NOT VERIFIED);
- judges used were validated (C3); if a judge fails validation mid-run ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE, not VERIFIED.

**Judge gate.** An LLM judge may gate only after TPR ≥ 0.9 **and** TNR ≥ 0.9 on the held-out test split (per `evals/references/judge-validation.md`). Prefer the `fuse` multi-model panel + majority aggregation (`harness-loop` eval-gate pattern) when single-judge TNR is weak.

**Cost / efficiency.** Tokens (in/out/cache) + $ per task per cell, from the eval-record cost block and `ctx stats`. A "cheap variant win" = composite within **ε = 0.03** of the full variant at **≥30% fewer tokens** on cheap cells.

**Regression gate** (`autoresearch.checks.sh`, exit≠0 ⇒ `status: checks_failed` ⇒ auto-revert): fails if any committed-baseline cell drops below `baseline − 0.02`, any deterministic contract breaks, or the **cache-stability canary** changes for a fixed model.

**Agnosticism check.** Adding a `(adapter, model, thinking)` cell to `matrix.yaml` and re-running must need **zero** code edits and produce a valid scorecard (this is a test, not a hope).

**Dynamic-variant check.** A contract eval (model the existing `skill-availability-delta` skillopt benchmark under `my-pi/extensions/skill-loader/eval/skillopt/`) asserts: (a) switching active model swaps the loaded variant correctly; (b) same-model same-cwd sessions keep `params.system` + `tools[]` byte-stable (cache canary).

**Auditability check.** For every promoted version: a committed scorecard file + a git commit + a `skill-workshop` proposal with `evidenceRefs`. `git log` + the scorecard dir must reconstruct the full improvement history per skill across model releases.

---

## §E — Architecture (grounded in existing tools)

Five components. Reuse first; the only **new code** is a small load-time variant resolver inside the existing `skill-loader` (Component C) — no new tool, no core patch.

**A. Eval contract + rubric/judge layer** — *extends `evals` + `skillopt`.*
- Per skill: `eval/<skill>/{rubric.md, cases/{train,val,test}.jsonl, judges/}`. Cases carry deterministic fields (`expected_refs`, `must_mention`, `must_not_mention`, `threshold`) as in `skill-optimizer/references/eval-loop-with-skillopt.md`.
- Judges validated per `evals/references/judge-validation.md` (binary criterion, human labels, TPR/TNR). Ensemble via `fuse` (Appendix). Aggregation via `harness-loop/references/eval-gate.md` (majority, P0 veto).
- The **eval-record contract** (`eval-record.schema.json`) is the agnostic seam — mirrors `evals/references/eval-summary-watch.md` (suite, tier, commit, model, durationMs, cases, passed/failed/flaky, cost{tokens,cache}, metrics, artifacts).

**B. Model-agnostic matrix runner** — *new glue, contract-based; orchestrated as a deterministic `pi-workflow`.*
- `matrix.yaml`: list of cells `{adapter, model, thinking, tier: frontier|mid|cheap, tags:[new-release?]}`.
- Orchestration via a **pi Workflow** (`my-pi/extensions/pi-workflow`): `parallel()` fans rollouts across cells; use **tier aliases** (`model:"fast"|"medium"|omit=flagship`) which resolve to the current model for that tier *on whatever provider is active* — so the matrix tracks new model releases automatically and the cheap/mid/frontier tiers are first-class. Cheap fan-out scouts → `"fast"`; the judge/synthesis step → flagship.
- Adapters (thin, swappable) all emit the eval-record contract:
  - `pi` adapter → headless `pi -p "<task>" --no-session` rollouts; ensembles via `fuse` presets.
  - `claude-code` adapter → `ultracode` orchestrator/worker combos (`UC_SELECTOR=0`, Appendix).
  - `codex` adapter → codex CLI (optional, proves 3-harness agnosticism).
- Output: scorecard matrix `skill_version × cell → {composite, pass_rate, cost, latency}`.

**C. Dynamic skill variants** — *extend the existing `skill-loader`; no new tool, no core change.* (Confirmed seam: the `skill` tool's `execute` does `body = readFileSync(found.filePath)` — one line; `DiscoveredSkill` has no variant fields and no model conditioning exists yet.)
- Variant model (data): each loadable file (parent `SKILL.md` **or** any `references/*.md`) may have a terser sibling, selected via a small map in frontmatter `metadata.variants` **or** a repo-level `skill-variants.json` keyed `(file, model-class, thinking) → variant file + justifying scorecard SHA`. Variant files are **excluded from ref enumeration** so the parent→child tree shape stays canonical. Most skills ship only a lite **parent router** (children shared, loaded on demand); add lite refs only for heavy children. Version-controlled in the skills repo; promoted via `skill-workshop`.
- Resolver (≈40–60 lines, all inside `skill-loader`): track active model via `session_start`→`ctx.model` + `model_select` (`event.model.provider/id`), thinking via `pi.getThinkingLevel()` + `thinking_level_select`; map model→class (frontier/mid/cheap) from config shared with the matrix tiers. Route **every skill-body read** through one `readSkillBody(filePath, model, thinking)` wrapper — exactly **3 call sites in `index.ts`**: the parent body in `skill.execute`, and the exact-child + recursive-child reads in `loadExactRefs`. That covers **single, multi (`child:[...]`), and parent→child/recursive** loads in one shot (the `/alias` slash commands route back through `skill({child})`, so no extra site). Record the chosen variant in result `details` for telemetry. `skill_search` unchanged.
- **Cache-safe + contract-stable by construction:** ref **enumeration stays canonical** (variant files filtered out of `listReferencesInDir`), so ref names, the parent→child tree, `skill_search` rows, and the `<available_skills>` listing (name + description) are **byte-identical** across models — the cached system prefix never changes per model. The variant only alters the **`skill()` tool result** (an appended message, never the cached prefix); served-body cost (`costLine`) is computed from the resolved variant at load time, so it stays accurate without touching cache. Lite variants lean harder on progressive disclosure (terse parent, detail in `references/`).

**D. Continual optimization loop** — *wraps with `autoresearch-*`.*
- A session per campaign: `autoresearch.sh` runs the matrix eval and emits `METRIC composite=<weighted across cells>` (+ per-cell secondary metrics); `autoresearch.checks.sh` = the §D regression gate; `autoresearch.jsonl` logs each candidate version with metric + `status` (keep/discard) + `asi` hypothesis.
- `skillopt train` proposes candidate edits → matrix eval → `verify-this` verdict → `skill-workshop apply` the winner → git commit. `ctx index` the run-record corpus so the loop can search prior results; `ctx stats` tracks context pressure as a secondary metric.

**E. Version control & provenance** — *git + `skill-workshop`.*
- One commit per promoted version; message links scorecard + autoresearch run id + judge verdict.
- Committed ledger: `eval/<skill>/scorecards/<date>-<cell>.json`. `skill-workshop` proposals carry `evidenceRefs` → scorecard + run ids; `apply` captures rollback.

```
                 ┌─────────────── matrix.yaml (frontier/mid/cheap × thinking × adapters) ───────────────┐
 skill vN ──►(B) runner ──►(A) deterministic asserts + (fuse) judge panel ──► eval-record per cell ──► scorecard
   ▲   │                                                                                                  │
   │   └──(C) variant loader picks vN-variant per active model ──(cache-stable)──┐                        ▼
   │                                                                              │            (D) verify-this verdict
   └──────── (E) skill-workshop apply + git commit  ◄── promote if VERIFIED ◄──── autoresearch keep/revert ◄┘
```

---

## §F — Phased plan (deliverable + verification each)

- **Phase 0 — Spec & pilot.** Pick 1 pilot skill; write `eval/<skill>/rubric.md` + ≥10 gold cases (train/val/test) + ≥1 judge. **Verify:** judge passes TPR/TNR on held-out test; `scripts/skillopt eval <bench> --mock` green.
- **Phase 1 — Agnostic matrix runner.** Build `eval-record.schema.json`, `matrix.yaml`, runner + `pi` adapter + `ultracode` adapter. **Verify:** scorecard for pilot across ≥3 cells × ≥2 thinking levels; adding a cell needs no code change (C5).
- **Phase 2 — Judge ensemble.** Wire `fuse` panel + majority aggregation; calibrate vs labels. **Verify:** panel TPR/TNR ≥ thresholds and ≥ best single judge; disagreement analysis committed (C3).
- **Phase 3 — Dynamic variants.** Extend `skill-loader`: model/thinking tracking + a load-time variant resolver in the `skill` tool; author ≥2 pilot variants; cache canary + selection contract eval. **Verify:** variant contract eval passes; `<available_skills>` byte-identical across models while the correct variant body loads per model (C7).
- **Phase 4 — Continual loop + provenance.** Wrap in `autoresearch`; integrate `skillopt train` → `verify-this` → `skill-workshop apply` → git. **Verify:** one full loop promotes a VERIFIED win and records it auditable; a planted-bad candidate is auto-reverted (C6, C8, C9).
- **Phase 5 — New-model drill + adherence.** Run §H drill; write runbook + CLI wrappers; hook into `weekly-review`. **Verify:** §H green; every recurring action has a wrapper with `--help`/dry-run/JSON (C11, C12).

---

## §G — Non-negotiables

1. **Agnostic by contract** — runner speaks `eval-record.schema.json`, never an SDK; harnesses/models are adapters + matrix cells.
2. **Cache golden rule** — variant selection deterministic per model; `params.system` + `tools[]` byte-stable within same-model same-cwd sessions (load `pi-cache-stability` before touching `skill-loader`).
3. **Progressive disclosure preserved** — parent-router + `references/` pattern intact; lite variants rely on it harder, never duplicate.
4. **No improvement claim without proof** — a committed scorecard + VERIFIED verdict, or it didn't happen.
5. **Deterministic before judge** — assertions dominate; LLM judges only after validation; judges are themselves evaluated.
6. **CLI/script wrappers for every recurring action** — enforce adherence + data flow; no tribal incantations.
7. **Reuse over reinvention** — extend `evals`/`skillopt`/`skillos`/`harness-loop`/`autoresearch`/`skill-workshop`; only a small load-time variant resolver inside the existing `skill-loader` is new code.

---

## §H — Final verification drill (proves the goal, not a phase)

Run start-to-finish, capture artifacts:
1. `run-matrix <pilot>` → baseline scorecard across all cells (committed).
2. Propose a candidate edit via `skillopt train`; `run-matrix` the candidate; confirm **VERIFIED** (§D) and `skill-workshop apply` + git commit with scorecard evidence.
3. Plant a deliberately-worse candidate; confirm **NOT VERIFIED** and auto-revert (`status: checks_failed` in `autoresearch.jsonl`).
4. **New-model drill:** add one `(adapter, model, thinking)` cell to `matrix.yaml`; re-run; confirm a valid scorecard with **zero code changes**.
5. Start two same-cwd sessions on different models; confirm the **correct variant loads each time** and the **cache canary is byte-stable** within each model.
6. `git log` + `eval/<pilot>/scorecards/` reconstruct the full improvement history with evidence.

Goal achieved ⇔ all six green and the §C checklist fully evidenced.

---

## §I — Risks & mitigations

- **Judge noise / single-model bias** → validate every judge (TPR/TNR); prefer `fuse` ensemble; deterministic weight dominates.
- **Cache breakage from variants** → deterministic per-model selection; cache canary in the regression gate; `pi-cache-stability` review.
- **Nondeterminism faking improvement** → n≥5 runs, spread non-overlap, INCONCLUSIVE verdict when noisy.
- **Cost blowups on big matrices** → tier the matrix (gate=cheap+1 frontier; periodic=full); `budget`/`triad` fuse presets for routine; `ctx` to cut context spend.
- **Scope creep into a framework** → contract + adapters only; pilot one skill end-to-end before generalizing.
- **Provider auth gaps** (OpenAI/codex for `cross` presets, `ultracode`) → keep mock smoke green; report missing env as a stop condition (per `skill-optimizer` stop conditions).

---

## Appendix — Tool reference (real paths / commands)

**autoresearch** (loop engine) — skills `autoresearch-create` / `autoresearch-finalize` / `autoresearch-hooks`. Session dir holds: `autoresearch.sh` (benchmark+scorer, prints `METRIC name=value`), `autoresearch.checks.sh` (post-iter gate, exit 0/≠0), `autoresearch.jsonl` (ledger: `{run, commit, metric, metrics{}, status: keep|discard|crash|checks_failed, asi{hypothesis,next_action_hint}}`), `autoresearch.md` (objective), `autoresearch.ideas.md` (backlog). Example session: `my-pi-monitor-esc-close-ui/`.

**evals / skillopt** — `skills/evals` (+ `references/judge-validation.md`, `promptfoo-evals.md`, `transcript-evals.md`, `eval-summary-watch.md`); `skills/skill-optimizer` → `scripts/skillopt targets|scaffold|eval [--mock]|setup|train`, `scripts/skills validate`; cases at `skillos/skillopt/<bench>/splits/*.jsonl`; existing seed benchmark at `my-pi/extensions/skill-loader/eval/skillopt/skill-availability-delta/`. `best_skill.md` = patch proposal, never wholesale copy. `skills/skillos` = traces→skills (Opik source of truth, `scripts/skillos validate`). `skills/harness-loop/references/eval-gate.md` = 3-judge majority JSON contract.

**fuse** — `~/.pi/agent/bin/fuse` (impl `my-pi-runtime/extensions/fusion/`). `fuse [--preset self-moa|anthropic-max|premium|budget|cross|cross-max|triad] [--pretty] [--save f.md] [--timeout sec] "<task>"`. Proposers fan out in parallel (personas/models), judge synthesizes. Output `FusionResult` JSON `{proposals[], analysis, answer, judgeText, meta{presetId,proposerModels,judgeModel}, diagnostics}`. Use as multi-model **judge panel** (triad/cross) or **candidate generator** (budget).

**ultracode** — `~/.local/bin/ultracode` (src `~/Projects/testing/UltraCode-Shim`). Proxy (`:8141`) launches Claude Code with chosen **orchestrator** + **worker** models. Non-interactive: `UC_SELECTOR=0` (+ config.json routes / selected model). Role: run the same task across Claude-Code model combos as matrix cells.

**pi-workflow** (deterministic orchestration) — skill `pi-workflow`; ext `my-pi/extensions/pi-workflow` (README has the globals surface). `Workflow` tool with `agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()`; each `agent()` forks a subagent. **Tier aliases** `model:"fast"` (cheapest/scaled-subagent), `"medium"` (mid), omit (orchestrator flagship) resolve to the current model per active provider — the runner's agnostic, release-tracking model selector. Role: orchestrate the matrix fan-out + the continual loop deterministically.

**context intelligence (`ctx` / context-mode)** — pkg `context-mode` (`~/.pi/agent/local-packages/context-mode-pi-stable/`). `ctx index <path>` (FTS5/BM25), `ctx search "<q>"`, `ctx stats` (tokens/$ saved), `ctx doctor`, `ctx insight`. Role: index run-record + skill corpus; track context pressure as a secondary skill metric (esp. for cheap-model variants).

**skill loading / variants** — `my-pi/extensions/skill-loader/src/{index.ts,skills.ts}`; docs `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md`. Scans `~/.pi/agent/skills/`, `<cwd>/.pi/skills/`, package `pi.skills`. `<available_skills>` listing (minimal/compact), `skill` + `skill_search` tools, parent→child progressive disclosure, `@file:` expansion. No variant support today → add a **load-time resolver in the existing `skill` tool** (`execute` swaps `found.filePath`→resolved variant; model from `session_start`/`ctx.model` + `model_select`, thinking from `pi.getThinkingLevel()` + `thinking_level_select`). No new tool, no core change; `skill_search` + the `<available_skills>` listing stay identical → cache-safe.

**skill-workshop** (governance/version control gate) — ext `my-pi/extensions/skill-workshop`; store `~/.pi/agent/skill-workshop/` (`proposals.json`, `proposals/<id>/{proposal.json,PROPOSAL.md,rollback.json,files/}`). Tools: `propose_create|propose_update|revise|apply|reject|quarantine|rebuild_manifest`; `autocapture` hook files proposals from durable corrections. Apply = atomic write + rollback capture. Proposals carry `evidenceRefs` → scorecards/run ids.

**verify-this** — `skills/development/references/verify-this.md`. Verdicts: **VERIFIED / NOT VERIFIED / INCONCLUSIVE**; falsifiable claim + baseline vs treatment + metric + threshold + confound check. This is the improvement-verdict primitive in §D.

content.text:
Here's the sharp version, grounded in what I just read in your repo: **you already own the immune system SuperAda had to invent.** Their genuinely-good engineering (gates, verdicts, version-controlled improvement, deterministic pipelines) you have as *primitives* — `autoresearch`, `verify-this`, `fuse`, `skill-workshop`, `pi-workflow`, the `harness-loop` eval-gate. The SEVH spec (`docs/goals/goal-agnostic-skill-eval-harness.md`) is literally the grounded version of the self-improvement loop they fake. Status: "build not started."

So the dogfood gap isn't *construction* — it's **activation under load**. You've never run a continual loop hard enough to stress the immune system. SuperAda did, badly, and learned what breaks. That's the thing to copy: run something real, continually, and let it break your gates.

## What to dogfood, ranked

**1. Activate SEVH on one pilot skill (the flagship dogfood).**
This is the antidote to SuperAda's #1 failure — ungrounded "extract learnings → rewrite memory" with no ground truth. Don't build the whole goal. Build **Phase 0 + 1 only**: one skill (`development/verify-this` or `code-review`, both already have eval scaffolding), ≥10 gold cases, one validated judge, the matrix runner across 3 cells, and the `autoresearch` loop running candidate→eval→verdict→promote/revert for ≥3 iterations unattended.
- **Falsifiable success (already specced in §C/§D):** one candidate edit returns VERIFIED and gets committed with its scorecard; one deliberately-bad candidate returns NOT VERIFIED and auto-reverts via `autoresearch.checks.sh`.
- **Why it's the truest dogfood:** it stresses the *entire* stack at once — skill-loader, cache stability, workflow fan-out, judge validation, the version-control gate. Whatever's fragile surfaces here.

**2. Build a loop/cron immune system for YOUR fleet (steal their best engineering).**
Your scheduled surface is now real — pi crons, `/loop`, `/schedule` routines, `autoresearch` sessions, claude-bridge across MacBook/lue-kube/openclaw. I found no health/orchestrator meta-layer (`loops.md` is a draft stub). SuperAda's Model Orchestrator + Health Report is the part worth copying wholesale.
- **Phase 1:** one cron that enumerates everything scheduled, flags `error` / stalled / never-ran / rate-limited, posts a digest. **Phase 2:** auto-retry with provider fallback (ties straight into your `claude-bridge-auth-map` and primary-model-availability notes).
- **Falsifiable success:** induce a failure (kill a session, force a 429) and the watchdog recovers-or-escalates before you notice. Steal their rollback-manifest-before-mutate discipline.

**3. Harden one fuzzy recurring task into a `pi-workflow` (your "Lobster" ladder).**
Their LLM-turn → typed-pipeline maturity ladder is exactly `ad-hoc /loop prompt → deterministic Workflow script`. Pick your most-run recurring agentic task, rewrite as a Workflow, measure variance + tokens before/after.
- **Falsifiable success:** same output quality, lower run-to-run variance, comparable-or-lower cost, and it's resumable. If it's *not* cheaper/more stable, that's a finding too.

**Two smaller ones, same logic (gate the thing SuperAda left ungated):**
- **Slop-gate autonomous output** — wire `slop-scan` as a gate on anything a loop emits (commits, PR text, memory writes). Success: blocks a planted slop sample, low FP on real output.
- **Grounded memory loop** — you already flag "verify the file/flag still exists before recommending." Automate it: an eval over `global-memory-eval-corpus.md` that scores memory writes for staleness. Counters their MEMORY.md drift directly.

## What NOT to copy
The content-spam crons (10× autonomous-blog, watercooler banter, influencer posts) and any reflection loop without a falsifiable gate. That's the burn-tokens-to-agree-with-yourself trap — and it's exactly what your `verify-this` + `autoresearch.checks.sh` exist to prevent.

My pick: **#1**. It's highest-leverage, it's already spec'd, and it converts your whole "prove it, then automate it" philosophy from doctrine into a running system. #2 is the better choice only if you specifically want the SuperAda-shaped operational win first.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/work-closeout

# Work Closeout

**Core invariant:** never end a repo-modifying session with anonymous dirty
state. Every changed file, stash, and WIP branch is completed, reverted, moved
to ignored scratch/backup with a reason, or linked to a GitHub issue/PR with
branch, commit, why-incomplete, next action, and verification state.

No naked dirty files. No anonymous stashes. No unlinked WIP branches.

## When to run

- Ending a session that modified repo state and not everything shipped.
- Handing off incomplete work to another agent/session/device.
- User says "closeout", "dirty triage", "wrap up but it's not done".
- Completed work that is ready to ship → use the `go` skill instead.

## Workflow

1. **Inventory** each repo touched this session:
   - `git status --short --branch`
   - `git stash list --date=local`
   - Cross-repo audit when several repos may be dirty:
     `node ~/Projects/personal/agent-race/scripts/agent-state.mjs snapshot --scan --focus work-closeout`
2. **Classify** every dirty file, stash, and local branch into exactly one bucket:

   | # | Bucket | Exit condition |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | Merged/done | Committed, pushed, PR/issue updated or closed |
   | 2 | Active PR | Branch pushed, PR (draft) open, checks known, next action recorded |
   | 3 | Tracked WIP | Branch pushed, issue links branch/commit/files, five fields filled |
   | 4 | Local scratch | Moved outside repo or to ignored path, reason recorded |
   | 5 | Reverted/deleted | Explicitly dropped as superseded/safe |
   | 6 | Preserved foreign | Untouched; likely owner + evidence recorded |

3. **Promote** non-trivial WIP (bucket 3): branch `wip/<scope>-<slug>` →
   commit `wip(scope): ...` → push → issue or draft PR carrying the five
   handoff fields. Draft PR when review/CI is useful now; issue when the
   branch is just a parking lot.
4. **Disposition stashes** — transport only, never storage. Name:
   `wip:<repo>:<issue-or-none>:<reason>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. A stash worth keeping
   gets an issue before session end; duplicates of committed work are dropped
   only with explicit approval.
5. **Branch & worktree hygiene** (run once per repo, after buckets 1–6 are
   dispositioned — never deletes unmerged/dirty/foreign state):
   ```bash
   git fetch --prune
   git config --global fetch.prune true            # set once
   # delete only fully-merged branches (-d self-protects); skip checked-out + load-bearing
   git branch --merged origin/main \
     | grep -vE '^[*+]|(^| )(main|runtime/stable)$' | xargs -r -n1 git branch -d
   # remove merged + CLEAN worktrees (never current, runtime/stable, or dirty/foreign)
   git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{p=;b=""} /^branch /{sub("refs/heads/","",);print p"\t"}' \
     | while IFS=$'\t' read -r p br; do
         [ "$(git -C "$p" status --porcelain|grep -c .)" = 0 ] \
           && [ "$(git cherry origin/main "$br"|grep -c '^+')" = 0 ] \
           && echo "safe-remove: $p [$br]"; done
   ```
   - **Entire shadow branches** (`entire/<sha>-<wt>`): never `git branch -D` them —
     that desyncs `.git/entire-sessions/` + `.entire/tmp/`. Prune via the tool:
     `entire clean --all --dry-run` then `entire clean --all --force`. Working-tree
     files survive (shadows are backups only); Entire re-creates on next session.
   - **Squash-merged branches** show as unmerged by `git cherry` (patch-id differs).
     Confirm landing with `gh pr list --state merged --search <branch>` before `-D`.
   - Worktree removal of a **clean + merged** tree is non-destructive and reversible;
     dirty or unmerged trees are bucket 3/6 — preserve, never auto-remove.
6. **Report** per repo: clean, or each preserved artifact with bucket + link;
   include branch/worktree counts before→after when hygiene ran.

## Five handoff fields (every preserved WIP)

1. Branch + commit
2. Issue / PR link
3. Why incomplete
4. Next action
5. Verification state (what ran, what didn't)

## Blocked or failing work

Capture the exact failing command / check URL / log excerpt; classify
(blocker, regression, flaky, infra, external/auth); create or update the
issue/PR with evidence, link, and next action plus required support.

## Foreign work

Dirty state that looks like another agent's: preserve it, never revert or
drop. Record likely owner from branch/stash names, `.pi/workspaces/`,
`.entire/logs/`. Material and untracked → open an issue or ask before touching.

## Hard rules

- Destructive dispositions (drop stash, delete branch, revert someone else's
  work) require explicit consent.
- Reporting "done" while a touched repo is dirty and undispositioned is an
  incomplete task.

Full policies and templates (stash/WIP-branch policy detail, failure and
handoff templates): references/incomplete-work-invariants.md — read when
promoting WIP, naming stashes, or writing failure/handoff artifacts.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/go

# /go

Announce at start: **"Using /go. Orchestrating verify → code-review polish → review gate → PR → CI-watch as clean-context subagents."**

You are the **orchestrator**. Phases run as sequential subagents except the review gate, which may fan out into parallel reviewers for non-trivial changes. File-based handoffs live in `./.go-output/`. The arc mirrors a manual ship cycle — clean up the diff, verify it works (surfacing regressions the request didn't ask about), get an independent review, open the PR, then watch CI and fix failures as they land — so the human can hand off the whole loop, not just the build.

`/go` prepares work for PR/CI; it does not merge. Use `land` when the ask is to babysit through merge and close out the session.

## References

| Phase | Handoff template |
|---|---|
| 1 Verify | `references/phase-1-verify.md` |
| 2 Code Review | `references/phase-2-code-review.md` |
| 3 Review gate | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md`; non-trivial fan-out also uses `references/phase-3-security.md` and `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md`; UI changes also use `references/phase-3-design.md`; evidence contract in `references/gstack-review-qa-ship-gates.md` |
| 4 PR | `references/phase-4-pr.md` |
| 5 CI watch | `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` |

Each handoff is self-contained: the subagent gets the file's contents (with `{{CWD}}` interpolated), reads the artifacts from prior phases, and returns a single-line STATUS.

## File workspace

```
.go-output/
  context.md      # Phase 0 writes — scope, classification, commands
  verify.md       # Phase 1 writes
  slop-scan.md    # Phase 1 writes when slop-scan is available (advisory)
  verify-*.png    # Phase 1 writes (screenshots)
  code-review.md  # Phase 2 writes
  code-craft.md   # Phase 3 writes (## Fixed + ## Follow-ups)
  security.md     # Phase 3 fan-out writes when security review runs
  test-review.md  # Phase 3 fan-out writes when test review runs
  design.md       # Phase 3 fan-out writes when the diff touched UI
  review-gate.md  # Phase 3 synthesis writes
  pr.md           # Phase 4 writes (PR URL + commits)
  ci-watch.md     # Phase 5 writes (CI result + any autofix commits)
```

Create the directory in Phase 0 and add `.go-output/` to `.gitignore` if absent — these are ephemeral.

## Phase 0 — Orchestrator setup

1. Capture scope:
   ```bash
   git status --porcelain
   git diff --stat
   # If tree is clean and commits exist on a branch:
   base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD main)
   git log --oneline "$base"..HEAD
   git diff --stat "$base"..HEAD
   ```
2. **Detect unrelated changes.** Compare the modified files against the user's stated work. Any file that doesn't fit the intent (for example a debug script when the user is shipping CSV export) is unrelated. If unrelated changes exist, halt before writing `context.md` and surface three options to the user: commit them on the current branch, stash them, or move them to a separate branch. Do not dispatch phases until resolved. Phases must never silently sweep unrelated work into the PR.
3. Classify the change as one or more of: `backend-cli`, `web-ui`, `desktop-native`, `refactor`.
   - **Determine `UI-touched`** — the single relevance gate for the Core Web Vitals trace (Phase 1) and the design review (Phase 3). Set `yes` only if the diff changes a rendered UI surface: components/templates/markup (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.html/.blade.php`), styles (`.css/.scss/.less`, Tailwind classes), or design tokens. Pure logic, API, config, test, build, or docs changes are `no` — even when the app has a UI. When `no`, Phase 1 skips the CWV trace and Phase 3 skips the design reviewer; never spin up browser/perf tooling for a change that can't move a pixel.
4. Derive project commands from `AGENTS.md` / `README` / `package.json` scripts / nearest config:
   - `TEST_CMD`, `LINT_CMD` (or `none`), `TYPECHECK_CMD` (or `none`), dev-server command if web-ui or backend-cli.
   - `SLOP_SCAN_CMD`: use `npm run review:slop` when present, otherwise `npx slop-scan scan . --lint` for JS/TS repos with `slop-scan` available, otherwise `none`.
5. Scan the user's prompt for context the phases should preserve: flaky-test warnings, known-broken tests on main, infra caveats, reviewer preferences. These go in the `Notes` field of `context.md`.
6. `mkdir -p .go-output` and write `.go-output/context.md`:

   ```markdown
   # /go context
   - Branch: <branch>
   - Base: <base-sha>
   - Classification: <kinds>
   - UI-touched: <yes|no>   # gates CWV trace (Phase 1) + design review (Phase 3)
   - Changed files:
     <list>
   - Test cmd: <cmd>
   - Lint cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Typecheck cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Slop-scan cmd: <cmd-or-none>  # advisory heuristic, not a standalone blocker
   - Dev-server cmd: <cmd-or-na>
   - Summary: <one-line intent suitable for branch slug + PR title>
   - Notes: <anything unusual>
   ```

7. Print: `/go context written: <N> files, classified <kinds>, dispatching verify subagent.`

## Phases 1–4 — Dispatch

For phases 1, 2, 4, and 5, dispatch a subagent with:
- **Prompt** = contents of that phase's reference file with `{{CWD}}` replaced by the absolute working directory.
- **Clean context** — do not carry parent conversation into the subagent.
- **Synchronous** — wait for the subagent to return before dispatching the next phase.

Harness mapping:
- **Claude Code** — `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"`.
- **Pi** — Pi's agent SDK with a fresh context.
- **Codex** — `SendMessage` to a spawned subagent, or Codex's native spawn mechanism.

After each return, read the phase's artifact file and the STATUS line. Apply the early-stop rules below.

### Phase 3 — Review gate with optional fan-out

Before Phase 3, classify whether this is **trivial**. Skip fan-out only if all are true:

- touches 2 files or fewer;
- diff is under 50 changed lines;
- does not touch auth, payments, data access, config, secrets, network boundaries, migrations, CI, deployment, or permissioning;
- Phase 1 found no verification gaps.

If trivial, run only `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` as the code-craft reviewer.

If non-trivial, dispatch these clean-context reviewers in parallel from the orchestrator:

| Reviewer | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Code craft | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` |
| Security | `references/phase-3-security.md` |
| Test engineer | `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md` |

#### Design review step (only when `UI-touched: yes`)

This is a first-class step of the review gate, not an optional extra. The rule is simple: **if `context.md` has `UI-touched: yes`, the design review runs; if `no`, it is skipped entirely.** It is gated on *touching UI*, not on diff size — a change small enough to be "trivial" in code terms (the video's like-button case) can still ship a contrast or layout-shift defect.

When `UI-touched: yes`, dispatch `references/phase-3-design.md` in parallel with the code reviewers above (it runs even when the code change is otherwise trivial). It consumes Phase 1's screenshots + Core Web Vitals and composes the `frontend` skill's `web-design-guidelines` and `taste-skill-anti-slop` references. A `DESIGN-NEEDS-WORK` verdict with unresolved blockers makes the gate `NO-GO`.

When `UI-touched: no`, do not dispatch it and do not load any browser/perf tooling — record `Design review: n/a (no UI surface)` in the synthesis.

Before synthesis, read `references/gstack-review-qa-ship-gates.md` when the diff is non-trivial, `UI-touched: yes`, or the gate must decide blocker vs follow-up from review findings.

Then synthesize their artifacts into `./.go-output/review-gate.md` with:

```markdown
## Decision
GO | NO-GO

## Required fixes before PR
<blockers with source artifact + file:line/evidence>

## Follow-ups
<non-blocking follow-ups>

## Rollback plan
<how to back out safely if this ships badly>
```

If any reviewer reports a blocker, stop before Phase 4 unless the fix is in-scope, applied, and the relevant tests are rerun green.

Before Phase 4 or final handoff, persist non-blocking follow-ups outside `.go-output/`: PR body/comment, GitHub issue, plan doc, repo notes, or the project's existing tracker. `.go-output/` is evidence, not the durable tracking surface.

### Phase 5 — Watch CI and autofix

After Phase 4 opens a PR on GitHub, dispatch `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` as an async CI babysitter and drive the PR to green. Passive CI waits use background Bash; failure interpretation and fix loops use background `Agent(general)` composing `autofix-pr`. Never foreground `gh pr checks --watch` from the orchestrator.

Skip Phase 5 only when:

- Phase 4 returned `PUSHED-NO-PR` (no GitHub PR to watch), or
- the repo has no CI checks (`gh pr checks` reports an empty set after the first poll), or
- the user asked for the PR to stay a draft / explicitly opted out of CI babysitting in their prompt (record in `context.md` Notes).

Phase 5 **never merges**. It stops at green and leaves the merge decision to the human. Unrelated/flaky failures are reported, not force-fixed (see the reference for the prefer-merge-main-over-bloat rule).

## Early-stop rules

- Phase 1 `BLOCKED` → stop. Surface `verify.md` to the user. Do not code-review or PR broken code.
- Phase 2 `BROKE-AND-REVERTED` → continue. The revert restored the green state from Phase 1.
- Phase 3 `NO-GO` or unresolved blocker → stop. Surface `review-gate.md` and the contributing reviewer artifacts.
- Phase 3 `REVIEW-FIXED` with failing tests → the subagent should have reverted; if it didn't, stop before Phase 4 and surface.
- Phase 4 `BLOCKED` → surface the reason (common causes: no `gh` auth, branch protection, dirty tree). Leave retry to the human. Do not run Phase 5 without an open PR.
- Phase 4 `PUSHED-NO-PR` → skip Phase 5 (nothing to watch); surface the remote + branch.
- Phase 5 `CI-RED` after its autofix attempts are exhausted → stop. Surface `ci-watch.md` with the remaining failing checks and their log evidence. Never merge a red PR; never `--no-verify` or force-skip a check to make it look green.

## Orchestrator finish

Print:

```
/go complete.
- Verify: <status>
- Code Review: <status>
- Review gate: <status>
- Design review: <status | n/a (no UI surface)>
- PR: <url>
- CI watch: <status> (green | red — <n> checks | skipped — <reason>)
```

Leave `.go-output/` on disk. The user can delete it when the PR merges. Any follow-ups from `.go-output/` must already be copied to a durable tracker before declaring `/go` complete.

## Guardrails

- If tests are already failing on `main` before /go starts, note it in `context.md`; downstream phases will not claim your change caused or fixed them.
- The human is the final gate. Never auto-merge.

Harness tooling per runtime + rationalizations to resist: `references/harness-notes.md` — read when selecting phase tooling or tempted to shortcut the gate.

Skill history: `references/changelog.md` — read when tracing a design decision.

`/go` is a full 5-phase orchestration (verify → review fan-out → PR → CI-watch). For a **draft** PR of Phase-0 scaffolding that already self-verifies (selfcheck green), the heavy multi-reviewer fan-out is overkill — I'll push + open the draft now and offer the full `go` review pass before you un-draft. skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/go

# /go

Announce at start: **"Using /go. Orchestrating verify → code-review polish → review gate → PR → CI-watch as clean-context subagents."**

You are the **orchestrator**. Phases run as sequential subagents except the review gate, which may fan out into parallel reviewers for non-trivial changes. File-based handoffs live in `./.go-output/`. The arc mirrors a manual ship cycle — clean up the diff, verify it works (surfacing regressions the request didn't ask about), get an independent review, open the PR, then watch CI and fix failures as they land — so the human can hand off the whole loop, not just the build.

`/go` prepares work for PR/CI; it does not merge. Use `land` when the ask is to babysit through merge and close out the session.

## References

| Phase | Handoff template |
|---|---|
| 1 Verify | `references/phase-1-verify.md` |
| 2 Code Review | `references/phase-2-code-review.md` |
| 3 Review gate | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md`; non-trivial fan-out also uses `references/phase-3-security.md` and `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md`; UI changes also use `references/phase-3-design.md`; evidence contract in `references/gstack-review-qa-ship-gates.md` |
| 4 PR | `references/phase-4-pr.md` |
| 5 CI watch | `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` |

Each handoff is self-contained: the subagent gets the file's contents (with `{{CWD}}` interpolated), reads the artifacts from prior phases, and returns a single-line STATUS.

## File workspace

```
.go-output/
  context.md      # Phase 0 writes — scope, classification, commands
  verify.md       # Phase 1 writes
  slop-scan.md    # Phase 1 writes when slop-scan is available (advisory)
  verify-*.png    # Phase 1 writes (screenshots)
  code-review.md  # Phase 2 writes
  code-craft.md   # Phase 3 writes (## Fixed + ## Follow-ups)
  security.md     # Phase 3 fan-out writes when security review runs
  test-review.md  # Phase 3 fan-out writes when test review runs
  design.md       # Phase 3 fan-out writes when the diff touched UI
  review-gate.md  # Phase 3 synthesis writes
  pr.md           # Phase 4 writes (PR URL + commits)
  ci-watch.md     # Phase 5 writes (CI result + any autofix commits)
```

Create the directory in Phase 0 and add `.go-output/` to `.gitignore` if absent — these are ephemeral.

## Phase 0 — Orchestrator setup

1. Capture scope:
   ```bash
   git status --porcelain
   git diff --stat
   # If tree is clean and commits exist on a branch:
   base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD main)
   git log --oneline "$base"..HEAD
   git diff --stat "$base"..HEAD
   ```
2. **Detect unrelated changes.** Compare the modified files against the user's stated work. Any file that doesn't fit the intent (for example a debug script when the user is shipping CSV export) is unrelated. If unrelated changes exist, halt before writing `context.md` and surface three options to the user: commit them on the current branch, stash them, or move them to a separate branch. Do not dispatch phases until resolved. Phases must never silently sweep unrelated work into the PR.
3. Classify the change as one or more of: `backend-cli`, `web-ui`, `desktop-native`, `refactor`.
   - **Determine `UI-touched`** — the single relevance gate for the Core Web Vitals trace (Phase 1) and the design review (Phase 3). Set `yes` only if the diff changes a rendered UI surface: components/templates/markup (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.html/.blade.php`), styles (`.css/.scss/.less`, Tailwind classes), or design tokens. Pure logic, API, config, test, build, or docs changes are `no` — even when the app has a UI. When `no`, Phase 1 skips the CWV trace and Phase 3 skips the design reviewer; never spin up browser/perf tooling for a change that can't move a pixel.
4. Derive project commands from `AGENTS.md` / `README` / `package.json` scripts / nearest config:
   - `TEST_CMD`, `LINT_CMD` (or `none`), `TYPECHECK_CMD` (or `none`), dev-server command if web-ui or backend-cli.
   - `SLOP_SCAN_CMD`: use `npm run review:slop` when present, otherwise `npx slop-scan scan . --lint` for JS/TS repos with `slop-scan` available, otherwise `none`.
5. Scan the user's prompt for context the phases should preserve: flaky-test warnings, known-broken tests on main, infra caveats, reviewer preferences. These go in the `Notes` field of `context.md`.
6. `mkdir -p .go-output` and write `.go-output/context.md`:

   ```markdown
   # /go context
   - Branch: <branch>
   - Base: <base-sha>
   - Classification: <kinds>
   - UI-touched: <yes|no>   # gates CWV trace (Phase 1) + design review (Phase 3)
   - Changed files:
     <list>
   - Test cmd: <cmd>
   - Lint cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Typecheck cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Slop-scan cmd: <cmd-or-none>  # advisory heuristic, not a standalone blocker
   - Dev-server cmd: <cmd-or-na>
   - Summary: <one-line intent suitable for branch slug + PR title>
   - Notes: <anything unusual>
   ```

7. Print: `/go context written: <N> files, classified <kinds>, dispatching verify subagent.`

## Phases 1–4 — Dispatch

For phases 1, 2, 4, and 5, dispatch a subagent with:
- **Prompt** = contents of that phase's reference file with `{{CWD}}` replaced by the absolute working directory.
- **Clean context** — do not carry parent conversation into the subagent.
- **Synchronous** — wait for the subagent to return before dispatching the next phase.

Harness mapping:
- **Claude Code** — `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"`.
- **Pi** — Pi's agent SDK with a fresh context.
- **Codex** — `SendMessage` to a spawned subagent, or Codex's native spawn mechanism.

After each return, read the phase's artifact file and the STATUS line. Apply the early-stop rules below.

### Phase 3 — Review gate with optional fan-out

Before Phase 3, classify whether this is **trivial**. Skip fan-out only if all are true:

- touches 2 files or fewer;
- diff is under 50 changed lines;
- does not touch auth, payments, data access, config, secrets, network boundaries, migrations, CI, deployment, or permissioning;
- Phase 1 found no verification gaps.

If trivial, run only `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` as the code-craft reviewer.

If non-trivial, dispatch these clean-context reviewers in parallel from the orchestrator:

| Reviewer | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Code craft | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` |
| Security | `references/phase-3-security.md` |
| Test engineer | `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md` |

#### Design review step (only when `UI-touched: yes`)

This is a first-class step of the review gate, not an optional extra. The rule is simple: **if `context.md` has `UI-touched: yes`, the design review runs; if `no`, it is skipped entirely.** It is gated on *touching UI*, not on diff size — a change small enough to be "trivial" in code terms (the video's like-button case) can still ship a contrast or layout-shift defect.

When `UI-touched: yes`, dispatch `references/phase-3-design.md` in parallel with the code reviewers above (it runs even when the code change is otherwise trivial). It consumes Phase 1's screenshots + Core Web Vitals and composes the `frontend` skill's `web-design-guidelines` and `taste-skill-anti-slop` references. A `DESIGN-NEEDS-WORK` verdict with unresolved blockers makes the gate `NO-GO`.

When `UI-touched: no`, do not dispatch it and do not load any browser/perf tooling — record `Design review: n/a (no UI surface)` in the synthesis.

Before synthesis, read `references/gstack-review-qa-ship-gates.md` when the diff is non-trivial, `UI-touched: yes`, or the gate must decide blocker vs follow-up from review findings.

Then synthesize their artifacts into `./.go-output/review-gate.md` with:

```markdown
## Decision
GO | NO-GO

## Required fixes before PR
<blockers with source artifact + file:line/evidence>

## Follow-ups
<non-blocking follow-ups>

## Rollback plan
<how to back out safely if this ships badly>
```

If any reviewer reports a blocker, stop before Phase 4 unless the fix is in-scope, applied, and the relevant tests are rerun green.

Before Phase 4 or final handoff, persist non-blocking follow-ups outside `.go-output/`: PR body/comment, GitHub issue, plan doc, repo notes, or the project's existing tracker. `.go-output/` is evidence, not the durable tracking surface.

### Phase 5 — Watch CI and autofix

After Phase 4 opens a PR on GitHub, dispatch `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` as an async CI babysitter and drive the PR to green. Passive CI waits use background Bash; failure interpretation and fix loops use background `Agent(general)` composing `autofix-pr`. Never foreground `gh pr checks --watch` from the orchestrator.

Skip Phase 5 only when:

- Phase 4 returned `PUSHED-NO-PR` (no GitHub PR to watch), or
- the repo has no CI checks (`gh pr checks` reports an empty set after the first poll), or
- the user asked for the PR to stay a draft / explicitly opted out of CI babysitting in their prompt (record in `context.md` Notes).

Phase 5 **never merges**. It stops at green and leaves the merge decision to the human. Unrelated/flaky failures are reported, not force-fixed (see the reference for the prefer-merge-main-over-bloat rule).

## Early-stop rules

- Phase 1 `BLOCKED` → stop. Surface `verify.md` to the user. Do not code-review or PR broken code.
- Phase 2 `BROKE-AND-REVERTED` → continue. The revert restored the green state from Phase 1.
- Phase 3 `NO-GO` or unresolved blocker → stop. Surface `review-gate.md` and the contributing reviewer artifacts.
- Phase 3 `REVIEW-FIXED` with failing tests → the subagent should have reverted; if it didn't, stop before Phase 4 and surface.
- Phase 4 `BLOCKED` → surface the reason (common causes: no `gh` auth, branch protection, dirty tree). Leave retry to the human. Do not run Phase 5 without an open PR.
- Phase 4 `PUSHED-NO-PR` → skip Phase 5 (nothing to watch); surface the remote + branch.
- Phase 5 `CI-RED` after its autofix attempts are exhausted → stop. Surface `ci-watch.md` with the remaining failing checks and their log evidence. Never merge a red PR; never `--no-verify` or force-skip a check to make it look green.

## Orchestrator finish

Print:

```
/go complete.
- Verify: <status>
- Code Review: <status>
- Review gate: <status>
- Design review: <status | n/a (no UI surface)>
- PR: <url>
- CI watch: <status> (green | red — <n> checks | skipped — <reason>)
```

Leave `.go-output/` on disk. The user can delete it when the PR merges. Any follow-ups from `.go-output/` must already be copied to a durable tracker before declaring `/go` complete.

## Guardrails

- If tests are already failing on `main` before /go starts, note it in `context.md`; downstream phases will not claim your change caused or fixed them.
- The human is the final gate. Never auto-merge.

Harness tooling per runtime + rationalizations to resist: `references/harness-notes.md` — read when selecting phase tooling or tempted to shortcut the gate.

Skill history: `references/changelog.md` — read when tracing a design decision.

skills.name: work-closeout
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/work-closeout

# Work Closeout

**Core invariant:** never end a repo-modifying session with anonymous dirty
state. Every changed file, stash, and WIP branch is completed, reverted, moved
to ignored scratch/backup with a reason, or linked to a GitHub issue/PR with
branch, commit, why-incomplete, next action, and verification state.

No naked dirty files. No anonymous stashes. No unlinked WIP branches.

## When to run

- Ending a session that modified repo state and not everything shipped.
- Handing off incomplete work to another agent/session/device.
- User says "closeout", "dirty triage", "wrap up but it's not done".
- Completed work that is ready to ship → use the `go` skill instead.

## Workflow

1. **Inventory** each repo touched this session:
   - `git status --short --branch`
   - `git stash list --date=local`
   - Cross-repo audit when several repos may be dirty:
     `node ~/Projects/personal/agent-race/scripts/agent-state.mjs snapshot --scan --focus work-closeout`
2. **Classify** every dirty file, stash, and local branch into exactly one bucket:

   | # | Bucket | Exit condition |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | Merged/done | Committed, pushed, PR/issue updated or closed |
   | 2 | Active PR | Branch pushed, PR (draft) open, checks known, next action recorded |
   | 3 | Tracked WIP | Branch pushed, issue links branch/commit/files, five fields filled |
   | 4 | Local scratch | Moved outside repo or to ignored path, reason recorded |
   | 5 | Reverted/deleted | Explicitly dropped as superseded/safe |
   | 6 | Preserved foreign | Untouched; likely owner + evidence recorded |

3. **Promote** non-trivial WIP (bucket 3): branch `wip/<scope>-<slug>` →
   commit `wip(scope): ...` → push → issue or draft PR carrying the five
   handoff fields. Draft PR when review/CI is useful now; issue when the
   branch is just a parking lot.
4. **Disposition stashes** — transport only, never storage. Name:
   `wip:<repo>:<issue-or-none>:<reason>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. A stash worth keeping
   gets an issue before session end; duplicates of committed work are dropped
   only with explicit approval.
5. **Branch & worktree hygiene** (run once per repo, after buckets 1–6 are
   dispositioned — never deletes unmerged/dirty/foreign state):
   ```bash
   git fetch --prune
   git config --global fetch.prune true            # set once
   # delete only fully-merged branches (-d self-protects); skip checked-out + load-bearing
   git branch --merged origin/main \
     | grep -vE '^[*+]|(^| )(main|runtime/stable)$' | xargs -r -n1 git branch -d
   # remove merged + CLEAN worktrees (never current, runtime/stable, or dirty/foreign)
   git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{p=;b=""} /^branch /{sub("refs/heads/","",);print p"\t"}' \
     | while IFS=$'\t' read -r p br; do
         [ "$(git -C "$p" status --porcelain|grep -c .)" = 0 ] \
           && [ "$(git cherry origin/main "$br"|grep -c '^+')" = 0 ] \
           && echo "safe-remove: $p [$br]"; done
   ```
   - **Entire shadow branches** (`entire/<sha>-<wt>`): never `git branch -D` them —
     that desyncs `.git/entire-sessions/` + `.entire/tmp/`. Prune via the tool:
     `entire clean --all --dry-run` then `entire clean --all --force`. Working-tree
     files survive (shadows are backups only); Entire re-creates on next session.
   - **Squash-merged branches** show as unmerged by `git cherry` (patch-id differs).
     Confirm landing with `gh pr list --state merged --search <branch>` before `-D`.
   - Worktree removal of a **clean + merged** tree is non-destructive and reversible;
     dirty or unmerged trees are bucket 3/6 — preserve, never auto-remove.
6. **Report** per repo: clean, or each preserved artifact with bucket + link;
   include branch/worktree counts before→after when hygiene ran.

## Five handoff fields (every preserved WIP)

1. Branch + commit
2. Issue / PR link
3. Why incomplete
4. Next action
5. Verification state (what ran, what didn't)

## Blocked or failing work

Capture the exact failing command / check URL / log excerpt; classify
(blocker, regression, flaky, infra, external/auth); create or update the
issue/PR with evidence, link, and next action plus required support.

## Foreign work

Dirty state that looks like another agent's: preserve it, never revert or
drop. Record likely owner from branch/stash names, `.pi/workspaces/`,
`.entire/logs/`. Material and untracked → open an issue or ask before touching.

## Hard rules

- Destructive dispositions (drop stash, delete branch, revert someone else's
  work) require explicit consent.
- Reporting "done" while a touched repo is dirty and undispositioned is an
  incomplete task.

Full policies and templates (stash/WIP-branch policy detail, failure and
handoff templates): references/incomplete-work-invariants.md — read when
promoting WIP, naming stashes, or writing failure/handoff artifacts.

## codedb
codedb is a code-intelligence and context tool — not your editor. Use it to understand the codebase before you change it: search, symbol/caller lookup, dependency graph, outlines, and codedb_context for task-shaped orientation. Make edits with your own native file tools. codedb_edit is only a fallback for clients with no native editing.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

## SEVH Phase 0 — Agnostic Skill Evaluation & Versioning Harness

Foundation for a **model-agnostic** skill eval/optimization loop: deterministic-first scoring + validated LLM judges, version-controlled improvements, dynamic skill variants per model-class. Spec: `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-agnostic-skill-eval-harness.md`.

This branch is the **clean isolation** of the SEVH work — cherry-picked off a polluted feature branch onto fresh `origin/main`, so it contains *only* the 4 SEVH commits and nothing else.

### What's built (this PR)
- **`sevh/` toolkit**
  - `core.py` — composite scorer + **§D verdict engine** (`VERIFIED` / `NOT VERIFIED` / `INCONCLUSIVE`); composite = `0.6·deterministic_pass_rate + 0.4·validated_judge_score` (judge weight 0 until validated).
  - `sevh` CLI — `selfcheck | test | score | verdict | lint-cases | validate-record | validate-matrix | scaffold | status | prices`.
  - 4 schemas — `eval-record.schema.json` (the agnostic seam), `rollout.schema.json`, `case.schema.json`, `matrix.schema.json`; `matrix.yaml` (8 cells); `prices.json` cost model.
  - `test_core.py`, examples/, README.
- **`eval/code-review/`** — pilot is **`code-review`** (locked): `rubric.md`, judge spec `polish-summary-judge.md`, 11 gold cases (train 4 / val 4 / test 3).

### Proofs (no API spend — all green)
- `sevh selfcheck` → §D engine **25/25**
- `python3 sevh/test_core.py` → **25/25**
- `sevh lint-cases code-review` → **11/11** gold cases valid

### Explicitly NOT done — gated on API-spend approval
- **C3 judge validation** (TPR ≥ 0.9 AND TNR ≥ 0.9) — `judges/labels.jsonl` has 3 seed labels only; needs real rollouts. Until validated, composite is deterministic-only.
- **Phase 1 matrix runner** across real model cells.

### Why draft
Phase 0 self-verifies (no-spend proofs green) but the harness can't earn a `VERIFIED` verdict on anything until the judge validates, which needs spend approval. Opening as a draft to land the scaffolding for review; un-draft after the judge-validation + matrix run (separate, spend-gated).
